models.opportunities: Each entry is a SaaS application inside the active project that has been scored as a 'Rip Opportunity' — the candidate for a Ravn build replacement. Includes the 0–100 score, the six factor sub-scores that produced it, redundancy callouts grouping overlapping tools, and an AI-generated build scope (narrative, feature list, integrations, tech stack, team, cost, and timeline).
models.factors: The six weighted inputs that combine into the Rip Score: Cost, Utilization, Feature Concentration, Pain, Replacement Tolerance, and Renewal Timing. Each carries its own weight; the weighted sum yields the headline score.
models.redundancyGroups: A categorical grouping of overlapping SaaS tools inside the same project — e.g. Slack and Microsoft Teams both sitting in the Communication category. Surfaces cumulative redundant spend.
models.buildScope: The AI-drafted plan for replacing this SaaS with a custom Ravn build. Includes narrative, complexity-tagged feature list, integrations grid, tech stack, team composition, USD cost range, and a week-by-week timeline.

relationships: Each Opportunity belongs to one Project (the project context is provided by the shell).
Each Opportunity has exactly six Factors that combine via weighted sum into the Rip Score.
Each Opportunity may sit inside zero or more RedundancyGroups when other apps in the same project share its category.
Each Opportunity optionally has one BuildScope — an opportunity without a build scope shows a 'Generate build scope' CTA.
BuildScope phases and milestones reference week numbers up to the BuildScope's totalWeeks.

opportunities.headline: Strong rip candidate — high spend, low utilization, contract due in 47 days.

factors.label: Cost
factors.evidence: $412K/yr at 320 seats — 2.1× the industry median per-seat for this segment.

factors.label: Utilization
factors.evidence: Only 142 of 320 licensed seats had a meaningful login in the last 30 days.
inputs: Source: Tool Intake survey + admin export

factors.label: Feature Concentration
factors.evidence: Power users touch 6 of the 47 modules included in the contract tier.
inputs: Modules used by ≥10% of active seats: 6
Most-used: Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities, Reports, Tasks, Email Sync
Unused premium tier add-ons: Einstein AI, CPQ, Field Service

factors.label: Pain
factors.evidence: 5 of 8 power-user respondents flagged 'flow customization complexity' as a daily blocker.
inputs: Recurring themes: customization complexity, slow page loads, admin bottleneck
Verbatim: 'Every change requires a ticket to our SF admin.' — VP RevOps
Verbatim: 'Reports are powerful but unreadable.' — Sales Manager

factors.label: Replacement Tolerance
factors.evidence: Champion identified inside RevOps; only Email Sync is considered hard-to-replace.
inputs: Switching-cost concern: Salesforce data export & retraining

factors.label: Renewal Timing
factors.evidence: Contract renews in 47 days — inside the 0–60 day decision window.
inputs: Auto-renewal clause: Yes (90 days notice already passed)
Procurement contact: Linda Chen, CFO Office

redundancy.summary: Two CRMs are in the project — sales is on Salesforce while marketing-led pipelines live in HubSpot.

buildScope.narrative: A Ravn replacement for Cloudwell's Sales Cloud footprint focuses on the six modules that power 92% of actual day-to-day work: Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities, Reports, Tasks, and Email Sync. The build is a single-tenant React + Postgres workspace with a custom-fields engine, Outlook bidirectional sync, and a lightweight forecasting view replacing Einstein. By scoping out unused enterprise modules and the customization tax, projected 5-year TCO drops from $2.4M to $680K while restoring the admin bottleneck to a self-serve workflow.

opportunities.headline: Hot — heavy macro reliance, 38% seat utilization, custom workflows already half-built outside Zendesk.

factors.label: Cost
factors.evidence: $168K/yr — Suite Professional tier with 90 paid agents.

factors.label: Utilization
factors.evidence: Only 34 of 90 agents touched a ticket last week.

factors.label: Feature Concentration
factors.evidence: 8 macros handle 71% of tickets — the long tail of Suite features is unused.

factors.label: Pain
factors.evidence: Support managers built a Notion-based escalation tracker because Zendesk SLAs are too coarse.
inputs: Verbatim: 'We do half our work in Notion.' — Support Lead

factors.label: Replacement Tolerance
factors.evidence: Macros and the help-center content can be migrated; Zendesk Talk integration is the sticky piece.

factors.label: Renewal Timing
factors.evidence: 112 days out — inside the typical 90-day decision window soon.

redundancy.summary: Zendesk owns ticketing but Notion + a Slack workflow are doing the work it was meant to do.

buildScope.narrative: A Ravn-built support workspace consolidates ticketing, the Notion escalation tracker, and the Slack workflow into one surface. Macros become typed, parameterized response templates; SLAs are configurable per-customer instead of per-tier; help-center content is imported as-is. Zendesk Talk telephony is wired through a thin Twilio adapter rather than rebuilt.

features.description: Multi-channel inbox across email, web form, and Slack.

features.title: Twilio Talk adapter

features.title: CSAT surveys
features.description: Post-resolution micro-survey embedded in email reply.

features.title: Reporting dashboard
features.description: Volume, SLA, CSAT, and per-agent throughput.

opportunities.headline: Warm — broad seat sprawl, but Notion is already eating the active workspace usage.

factors.label: Cost
factors.evidence: $84K/yr at 410 seats — modest per-seat but seat sprawl is the issue.

factors.label: Utilization
factors.evidence: 170 of 410 seats opened a page in 30 days; 240 sit dormant.

factors.label: Feature Concentration
factors.evidence: Wiki pages and meeting-notes templates account for almost all reads.

factors.label: Pain
factors.evidence: Search is the consistent complaint — answers exist but can't be found.
inputs: Verbatim: 'Confluence search is unusable.' — Eng Manager

factors.label: Replacement Tolerance
factors.evidence: No deep platform integrations; moving content is the only friction.
inputs: Integrations relied on: Jira issue links

factors.label: Renewal Timing
factors.evidence: Renewal sits 198 days out — outside the active decision window.

redundancy.summary: Confluence is the system-of-record but day-to-day docs increasingly live in Notion.

buildScope.narrative: A focused internal knowledge tool consolidates the Confluence wiki and Notion docs into a single workspace with first-class Jira issue linking. The build favors aggressive search (vector + keyword) and meeting-notes templates over Confluence's broad surface area.

features.title: Spaces & permissions
